subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in tools, plugin tools, client tools, and hooks?
rationale: This is both a product mode and a security boundary; automation cannot safely choose whether dry-run means plan-only, hook-after-policy, read-blocking, client-tool delegation suppression, or a broader Ask/Plan/Modify contract.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the no-side-effects semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, and embedded paths.

options.title: Fold into workflow modes
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer implementation until the broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent design chooses the shared vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Close the direction after deciding that scoped command-level dry-runs are safer than a global preview mode that users may mistake for a sandbox guarantee.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the no-side-effects semantics first, then implement a bounded core contract with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, and embedded paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal on the shared tool adapter and agent execution path where this boundary would need to be designed.
